issues.t: Optispark distributor misfires, stalls or won't start
issues.sym: The engine misses, idles rough, hesitates or stalls, often after rain, a car wash or a coolant leak. It may crank but not start, and the check engine light may come on.
issues.why: Both V8s use GM's Optispark distributor, mounted low on the front of the engine behind the water pump. Moisture or coolant gets inside, and the cap and rotor can crack or carbon-track. GM issued a service bulletin (87-65-27) for this miss on 1994-1996 Caprices with either engine.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Have a shop check the Optispark cap and rotor and look for a water pump leak above it; fix the leak at the same time so the new part isn't ruined.

issues.t: Water pump leaks coolant and the engine overheats
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, the level keeps dropping, you smell sweet coolant, or the temperature gauge climbs.
issues.why: The water pump is driven off the camshaft at the front of the engine. Its seal wears and the pump starts to weep, typically past 100,000 miles. The coolant often runs down onto the Optispark distributor below it.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and pull over and shut off the engine if it heads toward hot. Have the pump replaced soon, and have the Optispark checked for coolant damage at the same time.

issues.t: Oil leak from the front engine seals
issues.sym: Oil wets the front of the engine and the area around the distributor, with drips under the front of the car or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: Several seals sit at the front of the engine, including the seal behind the water pump drive and the crankshaft balancer seal. On these LT1 engines they harden with age and leak, and the oil can reach the Optispark.
issues.next: Check the oil level regularly and top it up. Have a shop find which seal is leaking; most of them mean removing the water pump and distributor, so it makes sense to do them together.

issues.t: Front lower ball joint nuts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, loose or wandering steering, or uneven tire wear. In the worst case a front wheel can collapse.
issues.why: On some 1996 Caprices the nuts holding the front lower ball joints to the steering knuckles were not tightened correctly at the factory. The joint can loosen, wear and separate from the knuckle, causing loss of control.
issues.next: Ask a Chevrolet dealer to run the VIN for recall 96V-018. If you hear a clunk or the steering feels loose, have the front end inspected before driving at speed.

issues.t: Wheel lug nuts may not be tight (recall)
issues.sym: A clicking or knocking from a wheel, a vibration, or a wheel that feels loose.
issues.why: Some 1995-1996 Caprices left the factory with lug nuts not tightened to spec. Loose nuts can let a wheel stud break and the wheel come off.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to run the VIN for recall 96V-245. If you hear clicking from a wheel, stop and check the lug nuts before driving on, and have them torqued to spec by a shop.

issues.t: Rear lower control arms can crack on police and taxi cars (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from the rear, the rear end feeling loose or steering itself, or visible cracks near where the rear sway bar bolts to the lower control arms.
issues.why: On heavy-duty police (9C1) and taxi (9C6) package Caprices, the rear lower control arm can crack at the sway bar mount and eventually break. Many ex-police 1996 Caprices are now in private hands.
issues.next: If your car is a former police or taxi car, ask a dealer to run the VIN for recall 96V-020 and have the rear control arms inspected. Don't drive hard on cracked arms.

issues.t: Engine stalls when shifted into reverse
issues.sym: The engine dies when you stop and shift into reverse, sometimes on wet pavement, and you lose power steering and brake assist while backing up.
issues.why: Owners of 1996 Caprices reported this stall to NHTSA, and GM issued a 1996 bulletin for a stall in reverse on these cars. Dealers sometimes reprogrammed or replaced the engine computer, with mixed results.
issues.next: Let the engine idle a moment before shifting into reverse, and be ready to brake firmly if it stalls. Have a shop scan for codes and check the idle air control and the bulletin's fix.

issues.t: 4L60-E automatic slips or loses gears at high mileage
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between shifts, harsh or late shifts, or loss of upper gears. Some owners notice a clunk as it drops into gear.
issues.why: The 4L60-E four-speed automatic is generally durable, but owners report wear-out problems on these cars beyond about 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it is slipping or burnt-smelling, stop towing or hard driving and get a transmission diagnosis; a rebuild is often needed.

issues.t: Transmission leaks at the rear output seal
issues.sym: Red fluid drips under the middle of the car, near where the driveshaft meets the transmission.
issues.why: The seal on the transmission's rear extension housing wears and leaks. RepairPal's owner reports put it at very high mileage, around 180,000-200,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and keep it topped up. A shop can usually replace the seal without removing the transmission.

issues.t: Fuel pump fails and the engine stalls
issues.sym: The engine sputters, jerks or backfires under load, stalls while driving, or cranks but won't start, especially after sitting.
issues.why: The in-tank electric fuel pump and sending unit wear out. Several 1996 Caprice owners reported pump failures to NHTSA, and the fuel gauge sender can also fail.
issues.next: If the engine stalls in traffic, steer to safety; steering and braking get heavy. Have the fuel pressure tested before replacing parts.

issues.t: Door window won't go up or sits crooked
issues.sym: A window binds, tilts in the frame, goes up slowly, or stops partway.
issues.why: The plastic rollers (sliders) that guide the glass in its track wear out and break. The door panel clips are also brittle by now.
issues.next: Keep the window closed if it might not go back up. A shop or a careful owner can replace the rollers; replace both in the door at the same time.

issues.t: Rust in rear quarter panels and frame
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or holes low on the rear quarter panels behind the rear wheels, rusty rear sway bar mounts, or flaking frame rails.
issues.why: Salted winter roads attack the lower rear body panels, and these body-on-frame cars also rust on the frame and rear suspension hardware.
issues.next: Have the frame rails and rear suspension mounts inspected on a lift, especially before buying. Surface rust can be treated; rot in the frame or mounts needs a body shop.

issues.t: EGR valve failure turns on the check engine light
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, and you may feel rough idle, hesitation or pinging under load.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation valve on these engines is known to fail, and GM issued service information about EGR valve problems on the Caprice.
issues.next: This is usually not urgent, but have the codes read. Pinging under load should be fixed soon because it can damage the engine.

issues.t: Electric air pump corrodes and fails
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, or you no longer hear the air pump whir for the first minute after a cold start.
issues.why: The electric air injection pump helps clean the exhaust after a cold start. When its check valves wear, moist exhaust gets back into the pump and corrodes it. GM issued a bulletin on water getting into the air pump.
issues.next: Not a safety issue, but it can cause an emissions failure. Have the check valves replaced along with the pump so it doesn't happen again.

issues.t: Serpentine belt chirps or power steering cuts out
issues.sym: A chirping or squealing belt, or steering that suddenly gets heavy, often at low speed when turning in and out of driveways.
issues.why: Owners reported belts that chirped or slipped and were replaced several times. A slipping or worn belt, tensioner or idler pulley can drop power steering assist.
issues.next: If steering suddenly gets heavy, slow down and steer firmly. Have the belt, tensioner and pulleys checked; a broken belt also stops the alternator from charging.

issues.t: Worn ball joints and fast front tire wear
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, loose or wandering steering, a pull to one side, and front tires wearing on the edges.
issues.why: These heavy cars wear their front ball joints and bushings, and several owners reported alignment and tire wear problems that kept coming back. Owners often upgrade to stronger ball joints.
issues.next: Have the ball joints and front end checked before an alignment. A badly worn ball joint can separate, so don't put it off if you hear clunking.

issues.t: Odometer display goes blank or flickers
issues.sym: The digital odometer reading fades, flickers or disappears.
issues.why: Solder joints on the odometer display board crack with age and heat.
issues.next: Not a safety issue. An instrument cluster repair shop can resolder the board. If you are buying one, be cautious if the odometer has been replaced or doesn't match the car's wear.
